This article runs the simulation study for configuration actg175_binary_m1_harm_fs3_effMinSG_both_n700_sims10 (study = ACTG175, outcome = binary, DGM = m1 [calibrated GLM, target OR(Q) = 2.0], objective = harm, FS bundle = fs3). See BUNDLE_PATH in the setup chunk for the exact bundle file used.

The article supports three rendering modes, controlled by sim_mode in the setup chunk:

  • import — load a pre-computed bundle (.rds) produced by a previous render in full mode. Fast.
  • demo — run the simulations inline at small N (100 + 100). Suitable for self-contained execution by readers who want to reproduce the workflow without committing to a full run.
  • full — run the simulations inline at production N and save the bundle to disk. Slow.
  • auto (default) — import if a bundle is present at the expected path, otherwise demo.

Data preparation, DGM calibration, and a single-trial sanity check always run, regardless of mode, so the tutorial narrative remains intact. In import mode the freshly-built DGM objects are overridden with the bundle’s versions to keep the OC tables consistent with the simulation output they describe.

library(foreach)

set.seed(8316951L)


# NB: BUNDLE_PATH and CONFIG_ID are defined in the `config-id` chunk
# at the top of the document so they can be referenced inline in the
# article-header prose.  Reused here without re-definition.

if (sim_mode == "auto") {
  sim_mode <- if (file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) "import" else "demo"
}
if (sim_mode == "import" && !file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) {
  stop(sprintf("sim_mode = 'import' but no bundle found at '%s'.",
               BUNDLE_PATH), call. = FALSE)
}

# -- Simulation control ------------------------------------------------------
# nsims_* are derived from sim_mode.  Edit the per-mode values here if
# different reference scales are needed.
nsims_alt <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L,            # not used (loaded from bundle)
  demo   = sims_demo,
  full   = sims_full,
  stop(sprintf("Unknown sim_mode: '%s'", sim_mode))
)
nsims_null <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L,
  demo   = sims_demo,
  full   = sims_full
)

cat(sprintf("sim_mode = %s | nsims_alt = %d | nsims_null = %d | sim_n = %d\n",
            sim_mode, nsims_alt, nsims_null, sim_n))
sim_mode = demo | nsims_alt = 10 | nsims_null = 10 | sim_n = 700

# -- Plot thresholds ---------------------------------------------------------
sgdist_min_pct_alt  <- 0
sgdist_min_pct_null <- 0

ordist_ylim         <- c(0, 4)

# Locals re-exposed for the single-trial sanity-check chunks

max_look <- fs_params$max_subgroups_search

  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion
)

1 Data Preparation

ACTG175 data prep (click to expand) 
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

# Binary outcome: adverse (failure to improve)
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 <= actg_df$cd40)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# -- DGM factor variables -----------------------------------------------------
# z1, z2: TRUE subgroup Q = {cd40 > 390 & wtkg > 81.2}
# Note that binary and continuous analyses are similar in identified subgroups
# (from observed-data FS result — see companion analysis document)

 actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$cd40 > 390, 1L, 0L))
 actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg > 80, 1L, 0L))

# z7-z12: truly binary indicators (no continuous counterpart)
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

actg_df$ar_naive   <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$str2 == 0, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$prior_6mo  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= 6 * 30.4375, 1L, 0L))

actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1)

# -- Analysis covariates (what the analyst sees) -------------------------------
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom","ar_naive","prior_6mo")
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.factor(actg_df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)

fs_params$selection_rule <- fs_selection_rule

# -- DGM variable sets ---------------------------------------------------------
dgm_factor_vars   <- c("z1", "z2", paste0("z", 7:12))
dgm_cont_vars     <- cont_vars
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)

# -- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
Q_n   <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N   <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_pct <- 100 * Q_n / Q_N

cat(sprintf("N = %d, Q prevalence = %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", Q_N, Q_n, Q_N, Q_pct))
N = 1083, Q prevalence = 113 / 1083 (10.4%)

    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 1]),

2 DGM Calibration

Target: OR(Q) = 2 on the adverse scale. The DGM includes factor variables (for subgroup definition) and raw continuous covariates (for a richer prognostic baseline), consistent with the survival generate_aft_dgm_flex() design.

Code 
dgm_calibrated <- calibrate_glm_interaction(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  target_effect   = cal_target_or,
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  effect_measure  = "OR",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  k_inter_range   = c(0, 3),
  grid_step       = 0.05,
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

3 Single Trial Sanity Check

Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand) 
df_sim <- simulate_from_glm_dgm(dgm_calibrated, n = sim_n, seed = 42)
Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand) 
itt_fit <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = "binomial", data = df_sim)
itt_OR <- exp(coef(itt_fit)["treat_sim"])
itt_event <- with(df_sim,mean(y_sim))

fs_params_single <- fs_params
fs_params_single$show_candidate_summary <- TRUE 

fs_single <- do.call(forestsearch, c(
  list(df.analysis = df_sim, confounders.name = confounders),
  fs_params_single
))

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) {
  fs_single_tabs <- sg_tables(fs_single, ndecimals = 3)
}

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )

  plan("sequential")
  timings <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-alt-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}

3 P: Pcons (consistency probability).

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is smallest-N within the effect-size band (sg_focus = “hrMinSG”) under the intersection of effect-band and Pareto-non-dominance rules. The effect-size band requires odds ratio within 10% of the maximum on the frontier (i.e., odds ratio >= 3.035). Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{wtkg <= 86.6} AND {cd40 <= 459.5} (odds ratio = 3.372, N = 91, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). This is the smallest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates. The Naive 95% CI for the odds ratio on this subgroup is (1.381, 8.233).

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • !{wtkg <= 84.8232} AND !{symptom} (odds ratio = 3.094, N = 109, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). Larger subgroup (N=109 vs N=91, 18 more subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker once the band is satisfied, so this candidate’s comparable effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • !{wtkg <= 84.8232} AND {cd40 <= 459.5} (odds ratio = 2.908, N = 110, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.908 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 84.8232} AND {cd40 <= 524.6} (odds ratio = 2.829, N = 123, Pcons = 0.970, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.829 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 84.8232} AND !{hemo} (odds ratio = 2.641, N = 128, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.641 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 84.8232} (odds ratio = 2.545, N = 135, Pcons = 1.000, K = 1). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.545 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 76} AND {cd40 <= 373.2} (odds ratio = 1.935, N = 167, Pcons = 0.940, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.935 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
fs_result <- fs
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs_result$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {

    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",

      show_message = TRUE
    )

  plan("sequential")
  timings <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}

3 P: Pcons (consistency probability).

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is smallest-N within the effect-size band (sg_focus = “hrMinSG”) under the intersection of effect-band and Pareto-non-dominance rules. The effect-size band requires odds ratio within 10% of the maximum on the frontier (i.e., odds ratio >= 2.136). Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{age <= 34.8} AND {ar_naive} (odds ratio = 2.374, N = 128, Pcons = 0.990, K = 2). This is the smallest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates.

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • !{age <= 34.8} AND {preanti <= 57} (odds ratio = 1.800, N = 142, Pcons = 0.900, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.800 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm$calibrated

  results_alt    <- bundle$results$alt
  results_null   <- bundle$results$null
  t_alt          <- bundle$meta$t_alt_sec
  t_null         <- bundle$meta$t_null_sec
  nsims_alt      <- bundle$meta$n_alt
  nsims_null     <- bundle$meta$n_null

  n_failed_null  <- bundle$meta$n_failed_null

  cat(sprintf("Imported bundle: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
  cat(sprintf("  config_id : %s\n", bundle$meta$config_id))
  cat(sprintf("  timestamp : %s\n", format(bundle$meta$timestamp)))
  cat(sprintf("  n_alt     : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_alt, n_failed_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  n_null    : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_null, n_failed_null))
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$package_version)) {
    cat(sprintf("  forestsearch %s\n", bundle$meta$package_version))
  }
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$config_id) &&
      bundle$meta$config_id != CONFIG_ID) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "Bundle config_id ('%s') does not match this article ('%s').",
      bundle$meta$config_id, CONFIG_ID
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Inline simulation complete (%s mode).\n", sim_mode))
}

5 Results

5.1 Metrics Glossary

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al. (2024, Section 3).

5.1.1 Detection

Found (\(\text{any}(Q)\)): proportion of simulations where the method identifies any harm subgroup (\(\texttt{any.H} = 1\)).

  • Under H1 (alternative): \(Q\) exists with a differential treatment effect. \(\text{any}(Q)\) is detection power.
  • Under H0 (null): \(Q = \emptyset\) and \(Q^c\) is the ITT population. \(\text{any}(Q)\) is the false positive rate (FPR) for falsely declaring that a harm subgroup exists.

5.1.2 Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true harm subgroup \(Q\) exists (\(Q = \{\text{cd40} > 421 \cap \text{wtkg} > 82.3\}\), prevalence \(\approx\) 10%) with a genuinely different treatment effect (OR(Q) = 2). Following León et al. (2024, Section 3), define for estimated subgroup \(\hat{Q}\):

\[ \text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}}, \quad \text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}}, \]

with analogous measures for the complement \(\hat{Q}^c\).

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

Table column León et al. notation Interpretation
Sen \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q})\) Fraction of true \(Q\) captured by \(\hat{Q}\)
Spec \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)\) Fraction of true \(Q^c\) correctly in \(\hat{Q}^c\)
PPV \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})\) Fraction of \(\hat{Q}\) truly in \(Q\)
NPV \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)\) Fraction of \(\hat{Q}^c\) truly in \(Q^c\)

Classification metrics are averaged across all simulations (León et al. 2024, Table 1). When no subgroup is detected (\(\hat{Q} = \emptyset\)), the simulation contributes \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0\) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0\) (since no member of \(Q\) is captured and no subjects are assigned to \(\hat{Q}\)). This convention is implemented at the source in run_simulation_analysis(), matching the original fs.estimates.out() function used in León et al. (2024).

NoteClassification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a \(\hat{Q}\) that captures “roughly the right region” but with slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV. Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised (oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing the true cuts in advance.

5.1.3 Classification Under H0

Under the null, \(Q = \emptyset\) — no subgroup with a differential treatment effect exists. The complement \(Q^c\) is the entire ITT population. Per León et al. (2024, Section 3), \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q})\) is undefined (shown as “—” in the table) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0\). For the complement, \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N\) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1\) since \(Q^c\) = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the detection rate (FPR).

5.1.4 Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are on the adverse scale: OR \(> 1\) = treatment (ZDV+ddI) increases the adverse outcome (non-improvement) = harm. No inversion or treatment switching is applied.

A ratio \(\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1\) indicates the method is recovering a subgroup close to the true size; values much smaller suggest FS is identifying a strict subset of \(Q\); values larger suggest FS is absorbing some \(Q^c\) subjects into \(\hat H\).

---
title: "ACTG175 Binary Harm Search: Simulation Study"
format: html
---

```{r config-id}
#| include: false

# Defined here (before prose) so the article-header citation below
# can refer to it via an inline `r` expression.  The main setup chunk
# (further down) reuses the same BUNDLE_PATH / CONFIG_ID variables.

sim_n <- 700

scenario <- c("actg175_binary_m1_harm")

fs_sg_focus <- "effMinSG"

# Default = "neighborhood" compatible with all sg_focus options
# but not pareto or both

fs_selection_rule <- "both"

# -- Build fs_params from sourced fs3 bundle ---------------------------
# Canonical FS parameter values are defined in _fsparams/fs3_params.R
# (including stop_threshold, which is returned as NULL when
# fs_sg_focus is hrMaxSG or hrMinSG per package constraint).

fs_tag <- "fs3"

source(sprintf("_fsparams/%s_params.R", fs_tag))
fs_params <- get(sprintf("get_%s_params", fs_tag))(sg_focus = fs_sg_focus)


# -- Mode --------------------------------------------------------------------
# One of: "import", "demo", "full", "auto".
# "auto" picks "import" if BUNDLE_PATH exists, else "demo".

sim_mode <- "demo"

sims_demo <- 10
sims_full <- 1000

sims <- sims_demo
if(sim_mode == "full") sims <- sims_full

BUNDLE_PATH <- sprintf(
  "%s_%s_%s_%s_n%d_sims%d.rds",
  scenario, fs_tag, fs_sg_focus, fs_selection_rule, sim_n, sims 
)

CONFIG_ID   <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(BUNDLE_PATH))

# -- FS parameters (sourced from canonical fs3 file) -------------------
# Canonical fs3 parameter values live in _fsparams/fs3_params.R.
# Edit there to apply changes uniformly across all sg_focus configs.


frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = c(1.0, 5.0),
  digits_effect = 2L,
  digits_pcons  = 2L,
  digits_ci     = 2L
)


n_workers   <- max(1L, floor(0.95 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

display_digits <- 3

```

This article runs the simulation study for configuration
**`` `r CONFIG_ID` ``** (study = ACTG175, outcome = binary,
DGM = m1 [calibrated GLM, target OR(Q) = 2.0], objective = harm,
FS bundle = fs3).  See `BUNDLE_PATH` in the setup chunk for the
exact bundle file used.

The article supports three rendering modes, controlled by `sim_mode`
in the setup chunk:

- **`import`** — load a pre-computed bundle (.rds) produced by
  a previous render in `full` mode. Fast.
- **`demo`** — run the simulations inline at small *N* (100 + 100).
  Suitable for self-contained execution by readers who want to
  reproduce the workflow without committing to a full run.
- **`full`** — run the simulations inline at production *N*
  and **save the bundle to disk**. Slow.
- **`auto`** (default) — `import` if a bundle is present at the
  expected path, otherwise `demo`.

Data preparation, DGM calibration, and a single-trial sanity check
always run, regardless of mode, so the tutorial narrative remains
intact. In `import` mode the freshly-built DGM objects are
overridden with the bundle's versions to keep the OC tables
consistent with the simulation output they describe.

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Setup and parameters (click to expand)"

library(forestsearch)
library(speff2trial)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(doFuture)
library(foreach)

set.seed(8316951L)


# NB: BUNDLE_PATH and CONFIG_ID are defined in the `config-id` chunk
# at the top of the document so they can be referenced inline in the
# article-header prose.  Reused here without re-definition.

if (sim_mode == "auto") {
  sim_mode <- if (file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) "import" else "demo"
}
if (sim_mode == "import" && !file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) {
  stop(sprintf("sim_mode = 'import' but no bundle found at '%s'.",
               BUNDLE_PATH), call. = FALSE)
}

# -- Simulation control ------------------------------------------------------
# nsims_* are derived from sim_mode.  Edit the per-mode values here if
# different reference scales are needed.
nsims_alt <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L,            # not used (loaded from bundle)
  demo   = sims_demo,
  full   = sims_full,
  stop(sprintf("Unknown sim_mode: '%s'", sim_mode))
)
nsims_null <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L,
  demo   = sims_demo,
  full   = sims_full
)

cat(sprintf("sim_mode = %s | nsims_alt = %d | nsims_null = %d | sim_n = %d\n",
            sim_mode, nsims_alt, nsims_null, sim_n))


# -- GRF standalone parameters ------------------------------------------------
grf_dmin           <- 0.10
grf_maxdepth       <- 2L
grf_sg_criterion   <- "mDiff"

# -- Reporting ---------------------------------------------------------------
sg_notation        <- "harm"

# -- Calibration -------------------------------------------------------------
cal_target_or      <- 2.0

# -- Diagnostic capture ------------------------------------------------------
diag_keep          <- c("fs_full", "candidate_table")
diag_keep_first_n  <- 5L

# -- Plot thresholds ---------------------------------------------------------
sgdist_min_pct_alt  <- 0
sgdist_min_pct_null <- 0
sgdist_top_k        <- 10L
ordist_ylim         <- c(0, 4)

# Locals re-exposed for the single-trial sanity-check chunks
c1       <- fs_params$hr.threshold
max_look <- fs_params$max_subgroups_search

grf_params <- list(
  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion
)
```

# Data Preparation {#sec-data}

```{r data-prep}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "ACTG175 data prep (click to expand)"

# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

# Binary outcome: adverse (failure to improve)
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 <= actg_df$cd40)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# -- DGM factor variables -----------------------------------------------------
# z1, z2: TRUE subgroup Q = {cd40 > 390 & wtkg > 81.2}
# Note that binary and continuous analyses are similar in identified subgroups
# (from observed-data FS result — see companion analysis document)

 actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$cd40 > 390, 1L, 0L))
 actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg > 80, 1L, 0L))

# z7-z12: truly binary indicators (no continuous counterpart)
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

actg_df$ar_naive   <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$str2 == 0, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$prior_6mo  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= 6 * 30.4375, 1L, 0L))

actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1)

# -- Analysis covariates (what the analyst sees) -------------------------------
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom","ar_naive","prior_6mo")
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.factor(actg_df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)

fs_params$selection_rule <- fs_selection_rule

# -- DGM variable sets ---------------------------------------------------------
dgm_factor_vars   <- c("z1", "z2", paste0("z", 7:12))
dgm_cont_vars     <- cont_vars
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)

# -- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
Q_n   <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N   <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_pct <- 100 * Q_n / Q_N

cat(sprintf("N = %d, Q prevalence = %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", Q_N, Q_n, Q_N, Q_pct))
cat(sprintf("Adverse rate: overall=%.1f%%, ZDV+ddI=%.1f%%, ddI=%.1f%%\n",
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 1]),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 0])))
```

# DGM Calibration {#sec-calibration}

Target: OR(Q) = `r cal_target_or` on the adverse scale.  The DGM
includes factor variables (for subgroup definition) and raw continuous
covariates (for a richer prognostic baseline), consistent with the
survival `generate_aft_dgm_flex()` design.

```{r calibrate}
dgm_calibrated <- calibrate_glm_interaction(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  target_effect   = cal_target_or,
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  effect_measure  = "OR",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  k_inter_range   = c(0, 3),
  grid_step       = 0.05,
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

cat(sprintf("\n  OR(Q):   %.3f (target: %.1f)\n",
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, cal_target_or))
cat(sprintf("  OR(Qc):  %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup))
cat(sprintf("  OR(ITT): %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall))
```

```{r null-dgm}
dgm_null <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "null",
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)
```

# Single Trial Sanity Check {#sec-single-trial}

```{r single-trial-alt-sim}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand)"
df_sim <- simulate_from_glm_dgm(dgm_calibrated, n = sim_n, seed = 42)
```


```{r single-trial-alt-analysis}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand)"

itt_fit <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = "binomial", data = df_sim)
itt_OR <- exp(coef(itt_fit)["treat_sim"])
itt_event <- with(df_sim,mean(y_sim))

fs_params_single <- fs_params
fs_params_single$show_candidate_summary <- TRUE 

fs_single <- do.call(forestsearch, c(
  list(df.analysis = df_sim, confounders.name = confounders),
  fs_params_single
))

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) {
  fs_single_tabs <- sg_tables(fs_single, ndecimals = 3)
}

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )

  plan("sequential")
  timings <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-alt-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}
```

```{r single-trial-alt-render-sg10}
#| echo: false
# Render sg10 candidate-summary table.  If fs_single$sg.harm is NULL the
# if-block returns invisible(NULL) and nothing is emitted.
if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) fs_single_tabs$sg10_out
```

```{r single-trial-alt-render-tab-estimates}
#| echo: false
# Render the formatted estimates table (gt).
if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) fs_single_tabs$tab_estimates
```

```{r single-trial-alt-render-bootstrap-table}
#| echo: false
# Render the bias-corrected bootstrap-results table (gt).
if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) summaries$table
```

```{r single-trial-alt-render-pareto-table}
#| echo: false
# Render the Pareto frontier table.  pareto_frontier_table() may return
# a gt_tbl (normal case), a data.table (fallback when gt is missing), or
# NULL (no consistency output).  All three behave correctly via auto-print.
if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  pareto_frontier_table(
    fs,
    ci_table      = ci_tab,
    digits_effect = frontier_params$digits_effect,
    digits_pcons  = frontier_params$digits_pcons,
    digits_ci     = frontier_params$digits_ci
  )
}
```

```{r single-trial-alt-render-explain}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Markdown explanation -- results: asis allows cat() output to flow through
# as markdown rather than being captured into a <pre> block.  Safe here
# because the explanation is intentional markdown.
if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) cat(explain_pareto_selection(fs, ci_table = ci_tab))
```

```{r fs-loo-setup}
# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
fs_result <- fs
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs_result$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo
```

```{r fs-loo-run}
#| eval: !expr run_loo

t0 <- proc.time()

# LOO is triggered by Kfolds = N (the function default behavior at
# forestsearch_cross_validation.R:109).  We pass it explicitly here for
# clarity.
N_loo <- nrow(fs_result$df.est)

fs_loo_result <- forestsearch_Kfold(
  fs.est        = fs_result,
  Kfolds        = N_loo,
  seedit        = analysis_seed,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_workers,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  details       = FALSE
)

plan("sequential"); gc(verbose = FALSE)
timings$loo <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nLOO completed in", round(timings$loo / 60, 2), "minutes",
    sprintf("(N folds = %d, n_workers = %d)\n", N_loo, n_workers))
```

```{r fs-loo-skipped-note}
#| eval: !expr skip_loo
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat("> **LOO skipped.** No harm subgroup was identified in the ",
    "full-analysis FS run (`fs$sg.harm` is `NULL`), so leave-one-out ",
    "cross-validation has nothing to evaluate.\n", sep = "")
```

### LOO Summary

```{r fs-loo-summary-text}
#| eval: !expr run_loo

cat(cv_summary_text(fs_loo_result, est.scale = "hr"), "\n")
cat(sprintf("Subgroup found in %.0f%% of %d folds.\n",
            100 * fs_loo_result$prop_SG_found, N_loo))
```

### LOO Tables

The `cv_summary_tables()` helper returns five publication-ready `gt`
tables. The first is the combined ITT + subgroup view; the next three
are component estimation tables (ITT, full-analysis subgroup, LOO
subgroup) that show the underlying treatment-effect estimates with
confidence intervals.

```{r fs-loo-tables}
#| eval: !expr run_loo

loo_out  <- forestsearch_KfoldOut(fs_loo_result, outall = TRUE,
                                  digits = construction_digits)
loo_tabs <- cv_summary_tables(
  loo_out,
  title    = "ACTG175 Leave-One-Out CV Summary (Binary, OR)",
  subtitle = sprintf("ITT and Subgroup Estimates: Full Analysis (FA) vs LOO (N=%d)",
                     N_loo),
  digits   = display_digits,
```

```{r fs-loo-tables-render}
#| eval: !expr run_loo
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Render each gt table in the list returned by cv_summary_tables().
# Mirrors the bootstrap-table rendering pattern used above
# (single-trial-alt-render-bootstrap-table) where the gt object sits as
# the last expression of its chunk.  Here cv_summary_tables() returns a
# *list* of tables, so we walk it explicitly and print each via
# htmltools::tagList(gt::as_raw_html(.)) -- gt's own knitr method
# only auto-prints when the gt_tbl is the chunk's final expression.
for (nm in names(loo_tabs)) {
  tbl <- loo_tabs[[nm]]
  if (inherits(tbl, "gt_tbl")) {
    cat(gt::as_raw_html(tbl), "\n\n")
  } else if (inherits(tbl, c("data.frame", "data.table"))) {
    # Fallback path if cv_summary_tables() returned a non-gt object
    print(knitr::kable(tbl, caption = nm))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

```{r single-trial-null-analysis}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Single simulated trial + FS analysis Null (click to expand)"

frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = c(1.25, 3.0),
  digits_effect = 2L,
  digits_pcons  = 2L,
  digits_ci     = 2L
)

itt_fit <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = "binomial", data = df_sim)
itt_OR <- exp(coef(itt_fit)["treat_sim"])
itt_event <- with(df_sim,mean(y_sim))

fs_params_single <- fs_params
fs_params_single$show_candidate_summary <- TRUE 


fs_single <- do.call(forestsearch, c(
  list(df.analysis = df_sim, confounders.name = confounders),
  fs_params_single
))

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) {
  fs_single_tabs <- sg_tables(fs_single, ndecimals = 3)
}

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

# Under the null DGM, the FS analysis typically produces no harm subgroup,
# so the entire bootstrap-and-rendering pathway below is a no-op.  The
# six-chunk structure (compute + 5 render) is kept symmetric with the
# alt-analysis section so the document scaffolding is uniform.
if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )

  plan("sequential")
  timings <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}
```

## Mode Handoff

```{r mode-handoff}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Bundle import or sim-result handoff (click to expand)"

if (sim_mode == "import") {
  bundle <- readRDS(BUNDLE_PATH)

  # Override the freshly-built DGMs with the bundle's versions so that
  # downstream OC tables match the simulation results they describe.
  dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm$calibrated
  dgm_null       <- bundle$dgm$null

  results_alt    <- bundle$results$alt
  results_null   <- bundle$results$null
  t_alt          <- bundle$meta$t_alt_sec
  t_null         <- bundle$meta$t_null_sec
  nsims_alt      <- bundle$meta$n_alt
  nsims_null     <- bundle$meta$n_null
  n_failed_alt   <- bundle$meta$n_failed_alt
  n_failed_null  <- bundle$meta$n_failed_null

  cat(sprintf("Imported bundle: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
  cat(sprintf("  config_id : %s\n", bundle$meta$config_id))
  cat(sprintf("  timestamp : %s\n", format(bundle$meta$timestamp)))
  cat(sprintf("  n_alt     : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_alt, n_failed_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  n_null    : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_null, n_failed_null))
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$package_version)) {
    cat(sprintf("  forestsearch %s\n", bundle$meta$package_version))
  }
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$config_id) &&
      bundle$meta$config_id != CONFIG_ID) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "Bundle config_id ('%s') does not match this article ('%s').",
      bundle$meta$config_id, CONFIG_ID
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Inline simulation complete (%s mode).\n", sim_mode))
}
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Metrics Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al.
(2024, Section 3).

### Detection

**Found** ($\text{any}(Q)$): proportion of simulations where
the method identifies *any* harm subgroup
($\texttt{any.H} = 1$).

- **Under H1** (alternative): $Q$ exists with a differential
  treatment effect.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is **detection power**.
- **Under H0** (null): $Q = \emptyset$ and $Q^c$ is the ITT
  population.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is the **false positive rate
  (FPR)** for falsely declaring that a harm subgroup exists.

### Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true harm subgroup $Q$ exists
($Q = \{\text{cd40} > 421 \cap \text{wtkg} > 82.3\}$,
prevalence $\approx$ `r sprintf("%.0f", Q_pct)`%)
with a genuinely different treatment effect (OR(Q) =
`r cal_target_or`).  Following León et al. (2024, Section 3),
define for estimated subgroup $\hat{Q}$:

$$
\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}},
\quad
\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}},
$$

with analogous measures for the complement $\hat{Q}^c$.

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

| Table column | León et al. notation | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Sen** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of true $Q$ captured by $\hat{Q}$ |
| **Spec** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of true $Q^c$ correctly in $\hat{Q}^c$ |
| **PPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}$ truly in $Q$ |
| **NPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}^c$ truly in $Q^c$ |

Classification metrics are averaged across **all** simulations
(León et al. 2024, Table 1).  When no subgroup is detected
($\hat{Q} = \emptyset$), the simulation contributes
$\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0$ and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0$
(since no member of $Q$ is captured and no subjects are
assigned to $\hat{Q}$).  This convention is implemented
at the source in `run_simulation_analysis()`, matching
the original `fs.estimates.out()` function used in
León et al. (2024).

::: {.callout-note}
## Classification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a
$\hat{Q}$ that captures "roughly the right region" but with
slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV.
Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised
(oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing
the true cuts in advance.
:::

### Classification Under H0

Under the null, $Q = \emptyset$ --- no subgroup with a
differential treatment effect exists.  The complement $Q^c$
is the entire ITT population.  Per León et al. (2024,
Section 3), $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ is **undefined** (shown
as "—" in the table) and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0$.
For the complement, $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N$
and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1$ since $Q^c$ = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the
**detection rate (FPR)**.

### Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are on the adverse scale:
OR $> 1$ = treatment (ZDV+ddI) increases the adverse outcome
(non-improvement) = **harm**.  No inversion or treatment
switching is applied.

# Operating Characteristics {#sec-oc}

## H1: Detection + Classification

```{r oc-alt}
format_oc_results(
  results_alt,
  metrics   = c("detection", "classification", "subgroup_size"),
  digits    = 2,
  digits_hr = 2,
  title     = "ACTG175 Binary: Harm Subgroup Identification",
  dgm = dgm_calibrated,
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation
)
```

### True Subgroup Sizes Across Replicates

```{r true-size-summary}
#| code-fold: true

# One row per replicate-method combination, but sizeH_true is identical
# across method rows within the same sim.  Deduplicate on sim.
truth_by_sim <- unique(results_alt[, c("sim", "sizeH_true", "sizeHc_true",
                                        "propH_true", "propHc_true")])

callout_Q <- sprintf(
  "|Q|:  mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))

callout_Qc <- sprintf(
  "|Qc|: mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))

cat(sprintf("True subgroup sizes across %d H1 replicates (N = %d each):\n",
            nrow(truth_by_sim), sim_n))
cat("  ", callout_Q,  "\n")
cat("  ", callout_Qc, "\n")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Reference sizes for the estimation tables below"}
- **|Q| (true harm subgroup)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))`).
- **|Qc| (complement)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))`).

Compare to $\widehat{|H|}$ (the FS-identified subgroup size) reported in
the row-group labels of the estimation tables below.  A ratio
$\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1$ indicates the method is
recovering a subgroup close to the true size; values much smaller
suggest FS is identifying a strict subset of $Q$; values larger suggest
FS is absorbing some $Q^c$ subjects into $\hat H$.
:::
